socfpga_iossm_ll.h

IOSSM low-level driver interface for the SoCFPGA bare-metal software stack.

Constants
Command types and sentinels

Command-type values and placeholders used when the driver builds a command request.

IOSSM_LL_NO_PARAM

No parameter register is written.

IOSSM_LL_CMD_TYPE_NO_OP

No-operation command type.

IOSSM_LL_TRIG_CNTRL_OP

Trigger and control command type. Used for the ECC commands.

IOSSM_LL_SYSTEM_INFO

System-info command type. Used with IOSSM_LL_GET_SYS_INFO.

IOSSM_LL_NO_TYPE

No IP type is specified.

IOSSM_LL_NO_ID

No instance id is specified.

ECC error injection

Parameter values and the data pattern used to inject an ECC error.

IOSSM_LL_SING_BIT_ERR_PARAM

Parameter for a single-bit ECC error.

IOSSM_LL_DBL_BIT_ERR_PARAM

Parameter for a double-bit ECC error.

IOSSM_LL_ERROR_DATA_VALUE

64-bit pattern written to DDR to trigger the injected error.

Command opcodes

Opcodes the driver sends to the IOSSM command interface.

IOSSM_LL_GET_SYS_INFO

Read system and interface information.

IOSSM_LL_ECC_EN

Enable ECC.

IOSSM_LL_ECC_EN_STAT

Read whether ECC is enabled.

IOSSM_LL_ECC_INT_STAT

Read the ECC interrupt status.

IOSSM_LL_ECC_INT_ACK

Acknowledge an ECC interrupt.

IOSSM_LL_ECC_INT_MASK

Mask ECC interrupts.

IOSSM_LL_ECC_WRBK_EN

Enable ECC write-back.

IOSSM_LL_ECC_GET_SBE_INFO

Read single-bit error information.

IOSSM_LL_ECC_GET_DBE_INFO

Read double-bit error information.

IOSSM_LL_ECC_ERR_INJ

Inject an ECC error.

IOSSM_LL_ECC_CLEAR_ERR

Clear the ECC error buffer.

IOSSM_LL_INSTANCE_OFFSET

The physical memory-mapped stride between consecutive IOSSM hardware instances.

Memory access status

Results from the DDR range and alignment checks. The read and write helpers return these before they touch memory that fails a check.

IOSSM_LL_MEM_OK

The address is inside the DDR window and is 8-byte aligned.

IOSSM_LL_MEM_ERANGE

The address is outside the DDR window.

IOSSM_LL_MEM_EALIGN

The address is not 8-byte aligned.

iossm_ll_req_payload_t

An intermediate software descriptor used to format the raw bitfields of an outgoing IOSSM command before it is committed to the hardware mailbox registers.

iossm_ll_response_t

Container for the three-word response payload returned by the IOSSM hardware upon completion of a command execution.

iossm_ll_desc_t

Software descriptor anchoring the context for a specific IOSSM hardware block.  This caches the resolved MMIO base address alongside hardware-queried ID values to minimize redundant bus reads during high-frequency ECC polling.

iossm_ll_read_reg32
uint32_t iossm_ll_read_reg32(
uint32_t 
base_addr,
uint32_t 
reg_offset
)

Performs a direct 32-bit Memory-Mapped I/O (MMIO) read from the IOSSM register space.  This centralized accessor facilitates easy replacement with test stubs or instrumentation tracing during debug.

Parameters
base_addr
uint32_t

The absolute physical MMIO base address of the target instance.

reg_offset
uint32_t

The specific 32-bit aligned register offset to read from.

Returns

The raw 32-bit hardware value read from the register.

Performs a direct 32-bit Memory-Mapped I/O (MMIO) write to the IOSSM register space.

Parameters

iossm_ll_safe_mem_write64
int32_t iossm_ll_safe_mem_write64(
uint64_t 
ddr_addr,
uint64_t 
value
)

Executes a strictly validated 64-bit write directly into physical DDR memory.  This is primarily utilized during error injection testing to flip bits in the memory array. The function enforces strict bounds checking against the known DDR window and guarantees 8-byte natural alignment to prevent bus faults.

Parameters
ddr_addr
uint64_t

Target physical DDR address.

value
uint64_t

The 64-bit value to write into memory.

Returns

IOSSM_LL_MEM_OK on success.  IOSSM_LL_MEM_ERANGE if the address falls outside the allowed DDR bounds.  IOSSM_LL_MEM_EALIGN if the address is not 8-byte aligned.

iossm_ll_safe_mem_read64
int32_t iossm_ll_safe_mem_read64(
uint64_t 
ddr_addr,
uint64_t 
*
out_value
)

Executes a strictly validated 64-bit read directly from physical DDR memory.  Applies the identical address boundary and natural alignment safeguards as the write equivalent.

Parameters
ddr_addr
uint64_t

Target physical DDR address.

out_value
uint64_t*

Pointer to a 64-bit integer to store the retrieved memory content.

Returns

IOSSM_LL_MEM_OK on success.  -EINVAL if the output pointer is NULL.  IOSSM_LL_MEM_ERANGE or IOSSM_LL_MEM_EALIGN if the address is invalid.

iossm_ll_send_command
iossm_ll_response_t iossm_ll_send_command(
const 
iossm_ll_desc_t 
*
desc,
uint32_t 
request,
uint32_t 
param
)

Constructs and issues a command sequence to the IOSSM hardware mailbox and actively polls for the corresponding response. This handles the low-level handshake required to trigger ECC scrubs, status queries, or interrupt acknowledgments.

Parameters
desc
const iossm_ll_desc_t*

Pointer to the populated IOSSM instance descriptor.

request
uint32_t

The specific command opcode (e.g., IOSSM_LL_ECC_INT_ACK).

param
uint32_t

The auxiliary parameter required by certain commands. Passed as 0 if unused.

Returns

A populated iossm_ll_response_t structure containing the 3-word response and the final hardware execution status.

Notes

This function blocks synchronously while polling the hardware response register.  Higher-level drivers must ensure appropriate timeouts or watchdog coverage to prevent deadlocks if the IOSSM IP hangs.

iossm_ll_err_inject_command
iossm_ll_response_t iossm_ll_err_inject_command(
const 
iossm_ll_desc_t 
*
desc,
uint64_t 
ddr_addr,
uint32_t 
param
)

Coordinates the multi-step hardware sequence required to inject an artificial ECC error. This function configures the IOSSM to expect a fault, utilizes iossm_ll_safe_mem_write64 to deliberately corrupt the physical memory at the target address, and fetches the resulting syndrome status.

Parameters
desc
const iossm_ll_desc_t*

Pointer to the populated IOSSM instance descriptor.

ddr_addr
uint64_t

The physical DDR address at which to inject the error.

param
uint32_t

The severity of the injection (IOSSM_LL_SING_BIT_ERR_PARAM or IOSSM_LL_DBL_BIT_ERR_PARAM).

Returns

A populated iossm_ll_response_t. If the address fails range/alignment validation, it immediately aborts and returns a zero-filled response (where the status field is 0).

iossm_ll_get_base_addr
int32_t iossm_ll_get_base_addr(
uint32_t 
instance,
uint32_t 
*
base_addr
)

Maps a logical IOSSM instance index to its absolute physical MMIO base address within the System-on-Chip.

Parameters
instance
uint32_t

The logical instance index (e.g., 0 or 1).

base_addr
uint32_t*

Pointer to a 32-bit integer where the resolved address will be stored.

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL if the instance index exceeds the available hardware blocks.
